title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter VII 'Analysis situs (troisième mouture)', June 1986. Grothendieck is axiomatizing an abstract 'figure geometry'. There is a set F of figures, an inclusion order ≤ ('sub-figure') and a refinement relation ≪. The previous page introduced the sup F∨G, the inf F∧G, the fine intersection F·G and the empty figure ∅_F.

Definitions on this page:
(1) M ⊂ F is the set of 'elementary figures' or 'multistrates'. They are defined as the strictly (sup-)irreducible elements of (F,≤), i.e. the completely join-irreducible elements. M carries the induced relations ≤ and ≪.
(2) A marginal arrow offers an alternative definition: M = the minimal elements of F∖{∅} for ≪.
(3) The strata of a figure F are the X∈M with X≤F, written X◁F ('X incident to F'). The 'déploiement' of F is the set of its strata, F̃ = {X∈M | X≤F}.
(4) L ⊂ M is the set of 'lieux' (points). The word is struck through.

Axioms, first group ('pure order' axioms). At1–At3 concern only (F,≤); At4–At7 will relate ≤ and ≪.
- At1: F ≠ ∅, and F has sups of all bounded families, of arbitrary index set I.
- At2: every figure is the sup of its strata, F = Sup_{X∈F̃} X.
- Margin: given At1, At2 is equivalent to the 'criterion of inclusion by strata': F≤G ⇔ ∀X∈F̃ ∃Y∈G̃ with X≤Y. Since G̃ is down-closed, this is the same as F̃⊂G̃.

Scholie: At1 and At2 should mean that F ↦ F̃ identifies F with a family F̃ of subsets of the poset M, satisfying:
- (a) every member is a closed set, i.e. a down-set;
- (b) every down-closed subset of a member is a member;
- (c) the members cover M, and F̃ ≠ ∅, so ∅ ∈ F̃.
An order-free variant is also given:
- (b') for each X∈M, the members containing X have a smallest one, X̃ (the principal down-set);
- (c') in (F̃,⊂) every bounded family has a sup.

Relations: F ≬ G ('compatible figures') iff F∨G exists, i.e. {F,G} is bounded above. Restricted to M, ≬ is reflexive, symmetric and inherited downward. Grothendieck then claims: in the finite-type case, with At1–At3, (F,≤) is reconstructed from (M,≤,≬). The next page states At3: pairwise compatibility of strata implies compatibility. F is then the set of finitely generated down-sets of M whose elements are pairwise compatible.

In modern terms this is a representation theorem. (F,≤) is a bounded-complete, coherent, prime-algebraic, finitary partial order. Equivalently, it is the domain of finite configurations of a prime event structure: events M, causality ≤, and conflict = complement of ≬, which is inherited upward. Geometrically the intended model is a stratified space: M = strata ordered by 'lies in the closure of', and figures = closed unions of strata, i.e. down-sets in the Alexandrov topology on the strata poset.
errors: Scholie condition (b) does not follow from At1+At2 with 'strictly irreducible' read as completely join-irreducible. Counterexample: the lattice M3 (bottom, three atoms a,b,c, top). The atoms are join-irreducible, and At1 and At2 hold. Yet {a,b} is a down-closed subset of the deployment of the top element and is not the deployment of any figure, since sup(a,b)=top has strata {a,b,c}. One needs complete primeness of the elements of M (X ≤ Sup F_i ⇒ X ≤ some F_i), i.e. a distributivity hypothesis. Equivalently, one must read 'strictly irreducible' as 'completely prime'. The 1981 Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel representation likewise uses complete primes rather than mere join-irreducibles.
The two proposed definitions of M (join-irreducibles for ≤ versus ≪-minimal elements of F∖{∅}) are different notions. The page links them with an arrow without reconciling them.
The reconstruction of (F,≤) from (M,≤,≬) also tacitly needs At3, the finite-type hypothesis, and the primeness above. Grothendieck flags At3 and finite type, but not primeness.

ideas.what: Elementary figures/multistrates as the irreducible elements of the poset of figures, and every figure as the sup of its strata
ideas.modern_name: Join-irreducible / complete-prime elements; (prime-)algebraic posets; Birkhoff-type representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1937) for finite distributive lattices; Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel (1981) for prime algebraic domains

ideas.what: Representing figures by their 'deployment' F̃ as down-sets of the strata poset (stratified-space intuition: closed unions of strata)
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov topology on the poset of strata; closed sets of a stratification as down-sets
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology/stratifications, but not this formalism

ideas.what: Compatibility relation ≬ (reflexive, symmetric, downward-inherited) and reconstruction of figures as finitely generated, pairwise-compatible down-sets of M
ideas.modern_name: Prime event structures (causality + conflict) and their configuration domains; coherent dI-domains; close to Girard's coherence spaces with an added order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen, Plotkin, Winskel (1981); Winskel (1980s); Girard (1987) for coherence spaces

ideas.what: Order-free characterization of the family of deployments (smallest member containing each point; bounded families have sups)

missed.claim: In building an axiomatic 'analysis situs' of figures and strata, Grothendieck independently arrives at what are essentially prime event structures / coherent prime-algebraic domains. These were introduced in theoretical computer science five years earlier: M = events/strata, ≤ = causality/closure order, ≬ = consistency, figures = configurations. The literature on tame topology and stratified spaces and the literature on concurrency and domain theory are not usually linked through this lens.
missed.quote: (F,≤) se reconstitue par (M,≤,≬), où ≬ satisfait X≬ réflexive symétrique; X≬Y, X'≤X, Y'≤Y ⇒ X'≬Y'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This offers a combinatorial-domain-theoretic model of stratified spaces, where closed unions of strata form a configuration domain. It may connect with the exit-path/poset-stratified-space viewpoint and with directed-topology models of concurrency. The link is mild and mainly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a fairly standard order-theoretic representation (complete primes, down-sets, coherence). It is already known from domain theory and event structures (1981), and the page contains a primeness gap. It is mildly notable that Grothendieck reinvented the event-structure/coherence-space formalism from a geometric (stratification) motivation in 1986.
transcription_corrections: 'Dans le cas où les figures sont de t.f.' should read 'de type fini' (consistent with the next page).
Marginal note at left middle reads roughly: 'F̃≠∅ indispensable si M≠∅, et dans tous les cas ∅∈F̃'. The transcription's 'nécessaire pour [?]' is uncertain.

The 'éléments minimaux de F∖{∅_F} pour ≪' clause is a separate right-margin alternative definition of M, linked by an arrow to 'figures élémentaires'. It is not a continuation of the 'strictement irréductibles' sentence.
'Axiomes "rien que nous"' is doubtful; it is more plausibly 'rien que ≤' / order-only axioms. The reading is uncertain.
